editorial:
You're dropped right back into the galaxy far, far away as Rey, Finn, and Poe Dameron race against time to stop the First Order's final push. The Resistance is running low on allies, but the spirit of the Jedi lives on through Rey's growing powers and the memory of those who came before. The vibe is big, loud, and packed with nostalgia, pulling you through hyperspace from one planet to the next with barely a breath. It feels like a grand finale trying to tie up every loose thread, and you can feel the weight of the whole saga pressing down on every scene.

The action scenes are fast and flashy, with lightsaber duels and space battles that look great on a big screen. Daisy Ridley gives it her all, and the chemistry between the main trio keeps things moving even when the plot gets messy. On the downside, the story rushes through big moments and leans hard on fan service, which can feel overwhelming. Still, if you grew up with these characters, you'll find plenty to enjoy.
endingExplained: Rey travels to the hidden planet of Exegol, where Emperor Palpatine has been secretly building a massive fleet. She confronts him in a final lightsaber duel, and with the help of the spirits of past Jedi, she defeats him once and for all. Ben Solo, formerly Kylo Ren, sacrifices himself to save Rey, and she takes the Skywalker name as her own. The Resistance wins, and peace returns to the galaxy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves epic space adventures and long-running sagas.
